name: Pembrolizumab
route_note: IV infusion every 3 or 6 weeks; subcutaneous form with berahyaluronidase alfa (Keytruda Qlex)
owner: Merck & Co. (MSD outside the US and Canada)

discovery.by: Organon scientists (Gregory Carven, Hans van Eenennaam, John Dulos)
discovery.note: Humanised IgG4 anti-PD-1 antibody; the programme passed to Merck through the Schering-Plough merger in 2009.

tagline: Anti-PD-1 antibody with the broadest label in oncology and top worldwide sales
summary: Pembrolizumab is a humanised IgG4 monoclonal antibody that blocks the PD-1 immune checkpoint. Approved in 2014 for melanoma, it now has dozens of indications across solid tumours and lymphoma and received the first tissue-agnostic cancer approval, for MSI-high or mismatch-repair-deficient tumours.
mechanism: Pembrolizumab binds PD-1 on T cells with high affinity and prevents its engagement by PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing an inhibitory signal that tumours exploit to suppress anti-tumour immunity.

Restored T-cell activity is greatest in tumours with pre-existing immune infiltration, high PD-L1 expression or high mutational burden, such as mismatch-repair-deficient cancers, which produce many neoantigens.
uses: Non-small cell lung cancer (first line, perioperative, adjuvant)
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma and primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma
Cervical, endometrial, gastric, oesophageal, renal cell and hepatocellular cancers
Cutaneous squamous cell and Merkel cell carcinoma

history.title: Antibody generated
history.detail: Organon scientists humanise the anti-PD-1 antibody later named pembrolizumab.

history.title: FDA accelerated approval
history.detail: Approved in September for advanced melanoma, the first PD-1 inhibitor approved in the US.

history.title: Lung cancer
history.detail: Approved for PD-L1-positive previously treated NSCLC.

history.title: First-line NSCLC
history.detail: KEYNOTE-024 shows superiority over chemotherapy in PD-L1-high NSCLC, leading to first-line approval.

history.title: Tissue-agnostic approval
history.detail: First FDA cancer approval based on a biomarker rather than tumour site: MSI-H/dMMR solid tumours.

history.title: Early-stage disease
history.detail: Approvals extend to high-risk early TNBC (KEYNOTE-522) and adjuvant renal cell carcinoma.

history.title: Best-selling drug
history.detail: Keytruda becomes the world's top-selling medicine by revenue.

history.title: Bladder cancer
history.detail: Approved with enfortumab vedotin for first-line advanced urothelial cancer.

history.title: Subcutaneous form
history.detail: FDA approves Keytruda Qlex, a subcutaneous formulation with berahyaluronidase alfa.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

serious: Immune-mediated endocrinopathies (thyroiditis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency, type 1 diabetes)

facts: In 2017 it received the FDA's first tissue-agnostic approval, based on MSI-H/dMMR status regardless of tumour origin.
Former US President Jimmy Carter was treated with pembrolizumab for metastatic melanoma involving the brain in 2015.
Key US patents are expected to expire around 2028, prompting the development of the subcutaneous form.
